title: PCA, ICA, and t-SNE
summary: Variance, independence, and a plot that is not a feature map.

choices.text: PCA finds orthogonal directions of largest variance. They are eigenvectors of the covariance, and the fit does not use labels.
The leading principal components are the directions that best separate the classes, so keeping them is a safe first step before any classifier.
ICA looks for sources that are statistically independent, not merely uncorrelated, and it relies on non-Gaussian structure. Unlike PCA, it does not rank components by how much variance they explain.
PCA and ICA return the same directions once the data are centered and whitened, because whitening removes the only difference between the two methods.
Classical t-SNE preserves global distances, so the gap between two clusters in the plot measures how far apart the groups are in the original space.
